findings.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:118 — `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining after `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`; when destinationCalendar is null/empty this throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration'). Old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`; should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

[High/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:255 — in updateEvent, the fallback branch `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only evaluated when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares cal.externalId against undefined/null and never matches, leaving selectedCalendar undefined and the update targeting an undefined calendarId; previously it fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId. Should be `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` (or match by credential).

[High/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315 — same tautological `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` in deleteEvent's else branch: calendarId resolves to undefined whenever externalCalendarId isn't passed, so cancellation/reschedule deletion of the calendar event fails (regression from `destinationCalendar?.externalId`).

[High/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — condition inverted: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, so orgs now get a slug immediately on cloud (billing-enabled, bypassing the requestedSlug/payment flow, whose condition was left unchanged) and get no slug on self-hosted installs; also unrelated scope creep for this PR, looks accidental.

[Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1080 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null (no eventType calendar and no organizer calendar); for a COLLECTIVE event where only teammates have destination calendars, all teammate calendars are dropped — the exact scenario this PR targets. Should initialize to [] instead of null.

[Medium/bug] packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 (likewise larkcalendar CalendarService.ts:128/163/192/237 and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156) — these services use destinationCalendar[0] (main host's calendar) regardless of which credential is executing, unlike Google's new credentialId matching; for collective events the 2nd+ host's credential posts to the first host's calendar ID → 404 (O365) or silently no event (Base filters the host's externalId out of the teammate's calendar list); multi-host collective only actually works for Google.

[Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~169 — `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops result.credentialId for non-calendar (video) results; the old code stored it on the booking reference (`credentialId: ... : result.credentialId`), where it's used to locate the video credential for later updates/deletions (e.g., Zoom); video references created after this change lose their credentialId.

[Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~380 — in createAllCalendarEvents' fallback branch (destination without credentialId), `createEvent(c, event)` is called without destination.externalId, so result.externalId is undefined and the booking reference is persisted with no externalCalendarId; combined with the CalendarService issues, later reschedule/cancel of such bookings can't target the right calendar (previously the reference got `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`).

[Medium/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:145 — when no destination matches credentialId (e.g., legacy destinationCalendar rows with null credentialId), createEvent silently falls back to "primary" instead of the selected calendar; previously it used destinationCalendar.externalId, so events can now land in the wrong calendar with no error.

[Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~528 — in updateAllCalendarEvents, the reschedule-merge deletion still uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))` (first reference only) while references are now plural; for collective bookings only one old calendar event is deleted and stale events remain on the other hosts' calendars.

[Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:~465 — in the recurring-cancellation branch, `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` deletes only the first calendar reference per booking; with multiple calendar references (collective), the other hosts' calendar events survive the cancellation.

[Medium/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts:175 — confirmation builds evt.destinationCalendar only from booking.destinationCalendar, and handleNewBooking persists only [0] (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`); so a COLLECTIVE booking requiring confirmation creates calendar events for only the first host when accepted, unlike the direct-booking path — the team-member aggregation logic exists only in handleNewBooking.

[Medium/data] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~730 — `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` was removed from the dynamic-booking user query in loadUsers; this is unrelated to the PR's purpose and any downstream logic reading user.organization for dynamic/org bookings now sees undefined; needs verification/justification.

[Low/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~382 — for destinations without credentialId, events are created on all credentials of that integration type; with multiple credential-less destinations of the same type (now possible), each credential creates an event per destination → duplicate calendar events.

[Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts:240 — drops the user-level fallback that every sibling handler implements (`booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar`); the old duplicated operand (`a || a`) was clearly a typo for the user fallback, and this handler now yields [] for legacy bookings without a booking-level calendar.

[Low/performance] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~345 — createAllCalendarEvents now awaits each destination sequentially and issues a per-destination prisma.credential.findUnique (N+1); collective bookings serialize N calendar API calls, increasing booking latency.

[Low/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts — the only test change is updating the expected payload to `destinationCalendar: []`; there is no coverage for the new multi-destination paths (credentialId matching, "primary" fallback, empty-destinationCalendar + Google Meet, collective push-when-null, multi-reference update/delete), so issues 1–3 would not be caught by the existing suite.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:118 — `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining after `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`; when destinationCalendar is null/empty this throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration'). Old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`; should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the new code destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without guarding for `undefined`. Since the diff shows multiple call sites now setting `destinationCalendar` to `[]` (e.g. booking reminders, webhooks, confirm/edit handlers), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` can be `undefined`, causing a runtime `TypeError` when `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. The previous optional chain `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` avoided this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:255 — in updateEvent, the fallback branch `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only evaluated when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares cal.externalId against undefined/null and never matches, leaving selectedCalendar undefined and the update targeting an undefined calendarId; previously it fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId. Should be `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` (or match by credential).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the new fallback computes `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the fallback branch), the `.find(...)` compares against `undefined/null`, so it will not match any real `cal.externalId`, yielding `undefined`. This is a regression from the previous fallback to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` and can result in `calendarId` being `undefined` for `calendar.events.update(...)` (or at least failing to select the intended destination calendar).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315 — same tautological `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` in deleteEvent's else branch: calendarId resolves to undefined whenever externalCalendarId isn't passed, so cancellation/reschedule deletion of the calendar event fails (regression from `destinationCalendar?.externalId`).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new `deleteEvent` (and similarly `updateEvent`) fallback computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is not provided (undefined/null), the `find` predicate becomes `cal.externalId === undefined`, so it will almost always return no match and thus `calendarId` becomes undefined. This is a regression versus the previous direct fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` and can break deletions/updates when callers don’t pass `externalCalendarId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1080 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null (no eventType calendar and no organizer calendar); for a COLLECTIVE event where only teammates have destination calendars, all teammate calendars are dropped — the exact scenario this PR targets. Should initialize to [] instead of null.

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the event is built with `destinationCalendar: ... ? [...] : ... ? [...] : null`, so `evt.destinationCalendar` can be `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team event types, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. With optional chaining, this is a silent no-op when `destinationCalendar` is null, so teammate destination calendars collected into `teamDestinationCalendars` are dropped in exactly that edge case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 (likewise larkcalendar CalendarService.ts:128/163/192/237 and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156) — these services use destinationCalendar[0] (main host's calendar) regardless of which credential is executing, unlike Google's new credentialId matching; for collective events the 2nd+ host's credential posts to the first host's calendar ID → 404 (O365) or silently no event (Base filters the host's externalId out of the teammate's calendar list); multi-host collective only actually works for Google.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and, for collective events, `handleNewBooking` appends teammates’ destination calendars after the organizer’s (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` then iterates over each destination/credential to create events. However, Office365/Lark/BaseCalendarService all destructure `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and use only that first entry’s `externalId` for `calendarId`/filtering, regardless of which credential is executing. This means when creating an event for a 2nd+ host’s credential, these services still target the first host’s calendar ID (likely 404 for O365/Lark, or BaseCalendarService filters out the correct calendar list), whereas Google’s service was updated to pick the destination calendar matching `credentialId`. This mismatch is directly visible in the diff and would break multi-host collective behavior for non-Google calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~169 — `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops result.credentialId for non-calendar (video) results; the old code stored it on the booking reference (`credentialId: ... : result.credentialId`), where it's used to locate the video credential for later updates/deletions (e.g., Zoom); video references created after this change lose their credentialId.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the reference object built after creating integrations changes `credentialId` from `isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` to `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` (and similarly later to `result.credentialId ?? undefined`). This verifiably drops `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results, whereas previously non-calendar (e.g., video) references would retain the credential id. The diff does not show any alternative place where video references’ credentialId is persisted, so this is a behavior regression that can break later lookups for updates/deletions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~380 — in createAllCalendarEvents' fallback branch (destination without credentialId), `createEvent(c, event)` is called without destination.externalId, so result.externalId is undefined and the booking reference is persisted with no externalCalendarId; combined with the CalendarService issues, later reschedule/cancel of such bookings can't target the right calendar (previously the reference got `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`).

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts createAllCalendarEvents(), when iterating destinations, the branch for destinations without credentialId does `destinationCalendarCredentials.map(async (c) => await createEvent(c, event))` and does not pass `destination.externalId` (even though the credentialId-present branch correctly calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`). Since CalendarManager.createEvent() now returns `externalId` only from that third argument and EventManager later persists `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`, this fallback path will produce booking references with missing/undefined externalCalendarId, making later update/delete unable to target the intended calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:145 — when no destination matches credentialId (e.g., legacy destinationCalendar rows with null credentialId), createEvent silently falls back to "primary" instead of the selected calendar; previously it used destinationCalendar.externalId, so events can now land in the wrong calendar with no error.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `createEvent` now selects `calendarId` via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and falls back to `"primary"` when no match is found. Previously it used `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.externalId` directly (single object), so an event with a chosen `externalId` but missing/NULL `credentialId` would still be inserted into that selected calendar. The diff also shows new call paths where `destination.credentialId` can be absent (e.g., `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` branch that handles `else` when `destination.credentialId` is falsy and calls `createEvent(c, event)`), which will trigger this fallback and can place events into the wrong calendar without error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~528 — in updateAllCalendarEvents, the reschedule-merge deletion still uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))` (first reference only) while references are now plural; for collective bookings only one old calendar event is deleted and stale events remain on the other hosts' calendars.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` within `updateAllCalendarEvents`, the code was updated to treat `calendarReference` as an array (`filter(...)`) and loops over all `_calendar` references to update them. However, in the reschedule-merge cleanup block (`if (newBookingId)`), it still does `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));`, which selects only the first calendar reference. With multiple calendar references now possible (e.g., collective/team bookings), this would delete only one old calendar event and leave stale events on other calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:~465 — in the recurring-cancellation branch, `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` deletes only the first calendar reference per booking; with multiple calendar references (collective), the other hosts' calendar events survive the cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, inside the recurring-event deletion branch the code still does `const bookingRef = updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` and then deletes only that single `uid`/`externalCalendarId`. With the diff’s refactor to support multiple calendar references (e.g., collective/round-robin) via `filter(...)` elsewhere, an `updBooking` can have multiple `_calendar` references; using `find` here will leave additional hosts’ calendar events undeleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts:175 — confirmation builds evt.destinationCalendar only from booking.destinationCalendar, and handleNewBooking persists only [0] (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`); so a COLLECTIVE booking requiring confirmation creates calendar events for only the first host when accepted, unlike the direct-booking path — the team-member aggregation logic exists only in handleNewBooking.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows COLLECTIVE team destination calendar aggregation was added only in `handleNewBooking` (it collects `teamDestinationCalendars` from `users.slice(1)` and later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` when `eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`). In contrast, `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts` now builds `evt.destinationCalendar` solely from `booking.destinationCalendar` (or `user.destinationCalendar`) as a single-element array, with no logic to add other hosts’ destination calendars or to use `schedulingType`. Additionally, `handleNewBooking` persists only the first destination calendar (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`), so subsequent flows that reconstruct `evt` from the booking (like confirm) cannot recover the full list. Given `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` iterates `event.destinationCalendar` to create events, this mismatch means confirmation acceptance will only create calendar events for that one destination calendar rather than all COLLECTIVE hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~730 — `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` was removed from the dynamic-booking user query in loadUsers; this is unrelated to the PR's purpose and any downstream logic reading user.organization for dynamic/org bookings now sees undefined; needs verification/justification.

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, the `loadUsers` branch that calls `prisma.user.findMany` no longer explicitly selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` (it was present before and is removed in the diff). Whether this causes a runtime bug isn’t verifiable from the diff alone because we can’t see what `userSelect.select` contains or any downstream reads of `user.organization`. However, it is a concrete, diff-grounded scope change unrelated to the destinationCalendar refactor and carries a real risk of changing the returned user shape for dynamic bookings unless justified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~382 — for destinations without credentialId, events are created on all credentials of that integration type; with multiple credential-less destinations of the same type (now possible), each credential creates an event per destination → duplicate calendar events.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, the new loop iterates over every entry in `event.destinationCalendar` (now an array). For a destination without `credentialId`, it executes `destinationCalendarCredentials = this.calendarCredentials.filter((c) => c.type === destination.integration)` and then creates an event for *each* credential of that integration (`Promise.all(...createEvent(c, event))`). Because this happens inside the per-destination loop, if there are multiple destinations of the same `integration` lacking `credentialId`, each credential will create one event per destination (i.e., duplicates). The diff also makes multiple destinations feasible (e.g., `handleNewBooking` pushes team member destination calendars into `evt.destinationCalendar` for COLLECTIVE scheduling), so the duplication scenario is exposed by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts:240 — drops the user-level fallback that every sibling handler implements (`booking.destinationCalendar || user.destinationCalendar`); the old duplicated operand (`a || a`) was clearly a typo for the user fallback, and this handler now yields [] for legacy bookings without a booking-level calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `requestReschedule.handler.ts`, the diff changes `destinationCalendar` from the (clearly erroneous) `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` to `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []`, which definitively removes any possibility of falling back to a user-level destination calendar. Other updated handlers in the diff (e.g., `confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`) explicitly fall back to `user.destinationCalendar` / `booking.user?.destinationCalendar`, so this handler will now produce `[]` for bookings lacking a booking-level destination calendar, breaking legacy/fallback behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~345 — createAllCalendarEvents now awaits each destination sequentially and issues a per-destination prisma.credential.findUnique (N+1); collective bookings serialize N calendar API calls, increasing booking latency.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents` was changed to `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and performs `await createEvent(...)` inside the loop, which serializes event creation per destination. Additionally, when a matching credential isn’t found in `this.calendarCredentials`, it does an `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` inside that same loop, creating a per-destination DB lookup pattern (potential N+1). This is a diff-grounded performance/latency concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts — the only test change is updating the expected payload to `destinationCalendar: []`; there is no coverage for the new multi-destination paths (credentialId matching, "primary" fallback, empty-destinationCalendar + Google Meet, collective push-when-null, multi-reference update/delete), so issues 1–3 would not be caught by the existing suite.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new multi-destination-calendar behavior (e.g., `destinationCalendar` becomes an array in types and event construction; GoogleCalendar `createEvent` now selects calendar by `credentialId`; EventManager now loops over multiple destinations and processes multiple `_calendar` references for update/delete; Meet fallback now only inspects the first destination). In contrast, the only shown test change in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts` is adjusting the expected webhook payload from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []`, with no added assertions/coverage for these new paths. That is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a direct functional defect.
